faq.title: FAQ
faq.subtitle: How AniKitty works, what features need an account, and what data the site collects.
faq.contactDesc: Join the Discord community or open an issue on GitHub. For account-specific requests (deletion, privacy), contact moderators there.

basics.whatIsA: AniKitty is a free anime streaming site with no subscription paywall. You can browse the catalog, watch episodes (sub and dub where available), and join community features when signed in. Lightweight click ads may appear on pages outside the player to help cover running costs (~€100/month). They never run in the video player or on profile pages. Ko-fi supporters can turn them off for their account. AniKitty does not host video files on its own servers — streams are resolved through third-party sources (via KittyAPI).
basics.accountA: No — you can browse and watch without signing in. An account unlocks your watchlist, synced watch progress across devices, episode comments, forum posts, live chat, public profiles, XP/levels, optional AniList import, and settings like 2FA. Sign up from the login button in the navbar.
basics.freeA: Yes. There is no paid tier. The player and profile pages stay ad-free. Lightweight click ads on other pages help cover the ~€100/month running cost. Donate €4+ on Ko-fi with your @username in the message for one month of ad-free browsing — larger tips extend your time.

watching.streamingA: When you open an episode, the player requests stream URLs through AniKitty's backend, which talks to KittyAPI. You can switch sub/dub and providers where available from the watch page. Progress is saved to your account when logged in.
watching.continueA: If you are signed in, the home page shows titles you started recently so you can jump back in. Progress is stored in the database and also cached locally in your browser for faster resume.
watching.anilistQ: Can I sync my list from AniList?
watching.anilistA: Yes. In Settings → Connected Accounts, connect AniList via OAuth. You can import your AniList library into your AniKitty watchlist.
watching.scheduleA: Schedule shows what is airing this week in your local timezone. Trending highlights popular and upcoming titles from the catalog feed.

accountSection.createQ: How do I create an account?
accountSection.createA: Click Log in in the navbar, switch to Sign up, and enter a username (3–10 letters/numbers), email, and password. Your password is hashed before storage.
accountSection.profileQ: What is on my public profile?
accountSection.profileA: Other users can see your avatar, banner, bio, role/level badges, watchlist lists, watch activity heatmap, and recent episode comments — unless you turn on Ninja mode in Settings → Privacy.
accountSection.ninjaA: Ninja mode hides your profile, watchlist, activity, and comments from everyone except you. Your username can still appear in live chat, forum, and episode comments.
accountSection.levelsQ: How do levels and XP work?
accountSection.levelsA: XP comes from watching episodes and posting episode comments. Levels unlock display roles/tiers on your profile, chat, and forum.
accountSection.twoFactorA: Optional TOTP can be enabled under Settings → Security. When enabled, login requires your password plus a 6-digit code.
accountSection.sessionsA: Settings → Security lists devices where you are logged in. You can revoke individual sessions or log out everywhere.

community.chatA: Live chat is real-time and requires an account. Messages auto-delete after a short time. You can edit or delete your own messages.
community.forumA: The forum is for longer discussions — threads and replies are stored until moderators remove them.
community.commentsA: On the watch page you can leave text and optional GIF comments per episode when signed in.
community.w2gA: Watch Together lets a host create a room code so friends sync the same episode.
community.onlineQ: What does the online counter mean?
community.onlineA: The online badge counts browser sessions that sent a heartbeat recently. It is not a list of logged-in usernames.

privacy.dataQ: What data does AniKitty store about me?
privacy.dataA: Account info (username, email, password hash, profile customization), watch data (watchlist, progress), community content (chat, forum, comments), session records, and preferences like Ninja mode.
privacy.browserQ: What is stored only in my browser?
privacy.browserA: Session cookie, player/UI settings, progress cache, online heartbeat ID, and level stats cache.
privacy.thirdPartyA: Google Analytics for page views, KittyAPI for streams, AniList if you connect, a lightweight click-ad network on pages outside the player, and external Discord/GitHub links.
privacy.notDoA: AniKitty does not sell your data and does not host video files on its servers. The video player and profile pages stay ad-free.
privacy.deleteQ: How can I delete my data?
privacy.deleteA: Go to Settings → Privacy → Account deletion to request permanent removal. You can also revoke sessions and disconnect AniList.
privacy.cookiesA: Sign-in uses an HttpOnly session cookie. Google Analytics may set its own cookies. The site enforces HTTPS in production.

support.adsA: Running AniKitty costs about €100 per month (servers, streaming, and database). Lightweight click ads on pages outside the player help cover that. They are not video ads and never run in the player or on profile pages.
support.disableQ: Can I turn click ads off?
support.disableA: Yes. Donate €4 or more on Ko-fi with your AniKitty @username in the message to get one month of ad-free browsing. Larger tips extend your time proportionally.
support.kofiA: No. The site is free for everyone. Ko-fi tips are optional but help cover running costs — €4 gives one month of ad-free browsing when you include your @username in the message.

security.passwordA: Passwords are hashed with bcrypt. Login issues a signed JWT in an HttpOnly session cookie.
security.httpsA: Yes — use the site over HTTPS. HTTP requests redirect to HTTPS in production.
security.rateLimitA: Sensitive actions are rate-limited by IP and/or user ID to reduce abuse.
security.moderationA: Admins and moderators can manage forum content, live chat, and user roles.
